metadata.title: Bill Gates's Top Second Quarter 2026 Move: Trims Berkshire Hathaway Inc at a -3.57% Portfolio Impact

content.text:
Bill Gates's Top Second Quarter 2026 Move: Trims Berkshire Hathaway Inc at a -3.57% Portfolio Impact
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Insights from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation Trust's Latest 13F Filing
Bill Gates (Trades, Portfolio), the co-founder of Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) and one of the world's most influential investors, recently submitted the 13F filing for the second quarter of 2026. The portfolio we track here, formerly known as Cascade Investment, has been managed as the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation Trust since June 2009. While an outside team manages the investments, Gates and his ex-wife guide proxy voting and exclude companies whose profit models conflict with the foundation's values. This quarter, the trust's most significant move was a substantial reduction in its largest holding, Berkshire Hathaway Inc (NYSE:BRK.B), signaling a notable shift in portfolio strategy.
Summary of New Buys
Bill Gates (Trades, Portfolio) added a total of 2 stocks to the portfolio during the quarter. The most significant addition was The Home Depot Inc (NYSE:HD), with 1,000,000 shares purchased, accounting for 1.02% of the portfolio and a total value of $352.68 million. The second largest addition was FedEx Freight Holding Co Inc (NASDAQ:FDXF), consisting of 1,192,181 shares, representing approximately 0.52% of the portfolio, with a total value of $180.02 million. These new positions suggest a modest but strategic diversification into consumer cyclical and industrials sectors.
Key Position Reduces
Bill Gates (Trades, Portfolio) also reduced positions in 2 stocks, with the most significant changes being:
-
Reduced Berkshire Hathaway Inc (NYSE:BRK.B) by 2,358,460 shares, resulting in a -13.83% decrease in shares and a -3.57% impact on the portfolio. The stock traded at an average price of $480.73 during the quarter and has returned 4.13% over the past 3 months and 0.27% year-to-date.
-
Reduced Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM) by 921,600 shares, resulting in a -3.33% reduction in shares and a -0.67% impact on the portfolio. The stock traded at an average price of $222.53 during the quarter and has returned 3.06% over the past 3 months and 3.05% year-to-date.
The reduction in Berkshire Hathaway is particularly noteworthy, as it remains the trust's largest holding at 21.35% of the portfolio. This trim could indicate a desire to rebalance risk or reallocate capital toward other opportunities, especially given the stock's relatively flat year-to-date performance. Similarly, the reduction in Waste Management, another core holding, suggests a cautious approach to mature, dividend-paying stocks in favor of potentially higher-growth opportunities.
